title: Further Limit General Fund Operating Budget
lastAction: Ref to the Com on Appropriations, if favorable, Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill lowers North Carolina's statutory cap on state General Fund operating budget spending from 7% to 6% of total state personal income. The change takes effect July 1, 2025, and applies to all future state budgets unless lawmakers vote by a two-thirds majority to exceed the new limit.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this bill constrains government spending growth and prevents the state budget from expanding faster than the state economy grows. They contend that a lower cap promotes fiscal responsibility, reduces the risk of unsustainable spending, and ensures taxpayer money is used efficiently without allowing automatic budget increases.
aiConArguments: Opponents argue that lowering the budget cap could restrict funding for essential services like education, healthcare, and infrastructure during times of economic growth. They contend that a stricter cap makes it harder to meet increasing population needs and may force difficult choices between important programs, while the two-thirds override requirement makes it cumbersome to address legitimate spending needs.
